messages:
jamie: quick alert — canary rollout of sdk v5 started ~5m ago, paging endpoints /v1/paging/* are returning 5xx for some clients. spikes in errors and streaming handshake failures. I’m tagging oncall.

andrew: I'm oncall, looking now. @deploy-bot can you paste the canary groups and recent deploy id?

deploy-bot: deploy started by ci/cd user 'release/v5.0.0' -> canary group 'canary-3' on 3 hosts (i-aaa, i-bbb, i-ccc). rolling at 2026-03-15T12:20Z. :rotating_light:

maria: I'm pulling logs — seeing client handshake rejects: 'unknown header client-proto-v' and 'nonzero paging offset' exceptions in runtime. probable API contract mismatch.

kevin: Confirmed. The sdk v5 adds 'X-Client-Proto: 5' header and changes streaming preface; servers expect older header 'X-Client-Ver'. Some proxies drop unknown headers causing handshake to fail and paging tokens to be parsed incorrectly.

andrew: Mitigation plan: 1) flip kill-flag to disable new header acceptance on servers (so they fallback to legacy parsing) 2) pause canary, 3) rollback if immediate fix not safe. Doing step 1 now.

sre-lead: Run:
```
# flip feature flag globally for canary group
redwood-ff set canary_accept_v5_header false --scope canary-3
```

sre-lead: Flag applied to canary-3 in 20s. Monitoring.

jamie: Traffic back to normal on 2/3 hosts, errors down from 8% -> 0.6%. Streaming sessions that had failed are reconnecting. Need to pause rollout to remaining host.

deploy-bot: pausing rollout per request by @andrew. Remaining hosts: i-ddd, i-eee.

andrew: I'll open rollback for canary to v4 artifact to be safe. @maria can you prepare a short customer-impact blurb? CS ops notified.

maria: Draft: "We observed increased 5xx errors and streaming disconnects for a subset of customers after a canary of SDK v5. We paused the rollout and implemented an emergency configuration to restore compatibility. Engineers are rolling back the canary artifact. No data loss reported."

customer-success: Notifying top 5 customers with active streaming sessions and offering status updates. Will paste customer list in thread.

jamie: Root cause hypothesis: SDK v5 changed client-server contract for stream preface and paging token format. Server-side parser is strict and rejects unknown header and non-zero offsets. We'll need either server compatibility layer or revert SDK change.

kevin: Short-term: rollback canary artifact on remaining hosts. Medium-term: add tolerant parser + e2e test that exercises v5 client handshake. Also add canary health checks that simulate v5 headers.

maria: ETA for rollback of canary group: 12 minutes. I'll coordinate postmortem owner — volunteering to own TL;DR and timeline. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: handoff scheduled — andrew -> jamie at 2026-03-15T13:00Z. :bell:

andrew: Update — rollback complete on canary group. Confirming no 5xx spikes in last 10m. Rolling back staged for next ring as well.

jamie: Action items: 1) PM/SDK to pause public release; 2) eng-runtime to add parser tolerant mode; 3) QA to add v5 handshake sim; 4) CS to message customers. Owner list in thread.

andrew: Severity set to Sev3 (customer-impacting, partial). Will escalate to Sev2 if degraded for >1h for major customers.

maria: Postmortem owners: maria, kevin. I'll open incident ticket INC-2026-401 and start a timeline.

kevin: We should also add a canary test that runs synthetic paging requests with both v4 and v5 token shapes and assert no 5xx.

jamie: Closing notes: thanks for quick triage. After postmortem we'll propose compatibility shim vs SDK rollback decision. :thumbsup:

customer-success: Top customers notified; a couple asked for immediate mitigation steps — pointed them to rollback info and temporary advice to pin to SDK v4.

andrew: marking this thread for follow-up and remediation plan in product board. If anything else pops, bump this thread.

maria: Incident ticket: INC-2026-401 created: https://internal.incidents/redwood/INC-2026-401 :spiral_note_pad:

kevin: leaving final note: observed paging token parse error stacktrace snippet:
```
error: invalid_paging_offset: expected 0 got 42
 at rpc.paging.Parser.parseToken (parser.go:213)
 at rpc.handler.handleRequest (handler.go:98)
```

jamie: last check — all green on canary ring, leaving throttled rollout paused. Will update once we have postmortem draft.

andrew: thanks all. Great coordination. :clap:
